doc.name: A — lounge furniture catalogue, hands in frame, 6-frame batch

config.text:
PRODUCT BRIEF — fill this in before running.
Product: bouclé lounge chair
Category: lounge furniture
Shot programme: hands in frame
Brand tone: [e.g. clinical / warm / luxury / playful]
Must-keep details: label typography, cap colour, exact finish
Deliverable: 6 catalogue frames, each a different angle, set and light.
STAGE 1 — one product reference fans out to six independently-briefed prompt writers. Each writer owns a different angle, set and lighting scheme.
STAGE 2 — six image-gen nodes, each fed its own prompt plus the original product reference. All six land in the download node.

config.system_prompt:
You are the visual lead responsible for this lounge furniture product library. This branch owns exactly one frame of a six-frame set: the in-context lifestyle in a hands in frame treatment.

SUBJECT. A bouclé lounge chair. Copy the product from the reference verbatim in form and finish. If a detail is unreadable in the reference, keep it neutral rather than inventing one.

CAMERA. Product in its real use environment with lived-in supporting props. Shoot on a 24mm wide at f/1.2, framing for a tight crop that breaks the subject at the frame edge.

LIGHT AND SURFACE. Key the frame with a projected gobo throwing a broken pattern across the background. Stage the product on or against brushed aluminium, and describe how that material reads under this light — its grain, reflectivity and the exact behaviour of the cast shadow.

COLOUR. Grade toward a Portra-style palette with creamy skin tones and soft greens. Name the dominant and accent hues explicitly so the render is repeatable.

TEXTURE. Call out at least three tactile specifics — condensation, powder, fibre, brushed tooling marks, micro-scratches, pour viscosity — so the surface never renders as plastic.

OUTPUT. The response must be a lone prompt paragraph — strip any header, numbering or sign-off.

config.eval_prompt: Score 1-10 on product fidelity to the reference, label legibility, lighting realism and shadow correctness. Reject any frame where the label text differs from the reference.
